papers.title: Learning Personalized Thermal Preferences via Bayesian Active Learning with Unimodality Constraints
papers.abstract: Thermal preferences vary from person to person and may change over time. The main objective of this paper is to sequentially pose intelligent queries to occupants in order to optimally learn the indoor air temperature values which maximize their satisfaction. Our central hypothesis is that an occupant's preference relation over indoor air temperature can be described using a scalar function of these temperatures, which we call the "occupant's thermal utility function". Information about an occupant's preference over these temperatures is available to us through their response to thermal preference queries : "prefer warmer," "prefer cooler" and "satisfied" which we interpret as statements about the derivative of their utility function, i.e. the utility function is "increasing", "decreasing" and "constant" respectively. We model this hidden utility function using a Gaussian process prior with built-in unimodality constraint, i.e., the utility function has a unique maximum, and we train this model using Bayesian inference. This permits an expected improvement based selection of next preference query to pose to the occupant, which takes into account both exploration (sampling from areas of high uncertainty) and exploitation (sampling from areas which are likely to offer an improvement over current best observation). We use this framework to sequentially design experiments and illustrate its benefits by showing that it requires drastically fewer observations to learn the maximally preferred temperature values as compared to other methods. This framework is an important step towards the development of intelligent HVAC systems which would be able to respond to occupants' personalized thermal comfort needs. In order to encourage the use of our PE framework and ensure reproducibility in results, we publish an implementation of our work named GPPrefElicit as an open-source package in Python.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文使用贝叶斯主动学习优化个体热偏好，与FEA代理模型或植入物设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA surrogate modeling, no implant biomechanics, no structural optimization, no uncertainty quantification for physical simulations.

summary_zh.motivation: 学习个体对室内温度的个性化偏好，减少查询次数。
summary_zh.method: 使用带单峰约束的高斯过程先验，通过贝叶斯推断和期望改进策略选择查询。
summary_zh.result: 相比其他方法，大幅减少观测次数即可学习最优温度。
summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，仅数值比较。

summary_en.motivation: To efficiently learn personalized thermal preferences of occupants with minimal queries.
summary_en.method: A Gaussian process prior with unimodality constraint is used to model the utility function, and Bayesian active learning selects queries via expected improvement.
summary_en.result: The method requires drastically fewer observations to identify the most preferred temperature compared to baselines.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; only synthetic numerical comparisons.

papers.title: Accurate prediction of melt pool shapes in laser powder bed fusion by the non-linear temperature equation including phase changes - isotropic versus anisotropic conductivity
papers.abstract: In this contribution, we validate a physical model based on a transient temperature equation (including latent heat) w.r.t. the experimental set AMB2018-02 provided within the additive manufacturing benchmark series, established at the National Institute of Standards and Technology, USA. We aim at predicting the following quantities of interest: width, depth, and length of the melt pool by numerical simulation and report also on the obtainable numerical results of the cooling rate. We first assume the laser to posses a double ellipsoidal shape and demonstrate that a well calibrated, purely thermal model based on isotropic thermal conductivity is able to predict all the quantities of interest, up to a deviation of maximum 7.3\% from the experimentally measured values.   However, it is interesting to observe that if we directly introduce, whenever available, the measured laser profile in the model (instead of the double ellipsoidal shape) the investigated model returns a deviation of 19.3\% from the experimental values. This motivates a model update by introducing anisotropic conductivity, which is intended to be a simplistic model for heat material convection inside the melt pool. Such an anisotropic model enables the prediction of all quantities of interest mentioned above with a maximum deviation from the experimental values of 6.5\%.   We note that, although more predictive, the anisotropic model induces only a marginal increase in computational complexity.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于LPBF熔池形状的热模拟，未涉及多孔结构、应力遮挡或生物医学植入物力学性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover porous structure design, stress shielding, fatigue testing, or osseointegration; it focuses solely on melt pool thermal simulation without biomedical context.

summary_zh.motivation: 验证LPBF熔池形状的物理模型，提高预测精度。
summary_zh.method: 采用各向异性热导率模型模拟熔池对流，对比各向同性模型。
summary_zh.result: 各向异性模型将熔池尺寸预测偏差从19.3%降至6.5%。
summary_zh.validation: 与NIST基准实验数据对比验证。

summary_en.motivation: To validate a physical model for predicting melt pool geometry in LPBF with high accuracy.
summary_en.method: A transient thermal model with anisotropic conductivity was used to approximate melt pool convection, compared against isotropic and measured laser profile models.
summary_en.result: The anisotropic model reduced prediction deviation to 6.5%, outperforming the isotropic model (7.3%) and the measured-profile model (19.3%).
summary_en.validation: Validated against experimental data from the NIST AMB2018-02 benchmark.

papers.title: Latent Simplex Position Model: High Dimensional Multi-view Clustering with Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: High dimensional data often contain multiple facets, and several clustering patterns can co-exist under different variable subspaces, also known as the views. While multi-view clustering algorithms were proposed, the uncertainty quantification remains difficult --- a particular challenge is in the high complexity of estimating the cluster assignment probability under each view, and sharing information among views. In this article, we propose an approximate Bayes approach --- treating the similarity matrices generated over the views as rough first-stage estimates for the co-assignment probabilities; in its Kullback-Leibler neighborhood, we obtain a refined low-rank matrix, formed by the pairwise product of simplex coordinates. Interestingly, each simplex coordinate directly encodes the cluster assignment uncertainty. For multi-view clustering, we let each view draw a parameterization from a few candidates, leading to dimension reduction. With high model flexibility, the estimation can be efficiently carried out as a continuous optimization problem, hence enjoys gradient-based computation. The theory establishes the connection of this model to a random partition distribution under multiple views. Compared to single-view clustering approaches, substantially more interpretable results are obtained when clustering brains from a human traumatic brain injury study, using high-dimensional gene expression data.   KEY WORDS: Co-regularized Clustering, Consensus, PAC-Bayes, Random Cluster Graph, Variable Selection

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文聚焦于高维多视角聚类与不确定性量化，与有限元代理建模或植入物设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses multi-view clustering with uncertainty quantification, but does not involve finite element analysis, surrogate modeling, or any biomechanical/structural optimization context.

summary_zh.motivation: 高维数据多视角聚类中不确定性量化困难
summary_zh.method: 提出潜在单纯形位置模型，通过KL散度优化实现近似贝叶斯推断
summary_zh.result: 在脑损伤基因表达数据上获得更可解释的聚类结果
summary_zh.validation: 在真实基因表达数据集上验证

summary_en.motivation: Uncertainty quantification in multi-view clustering of high-dimensional data remains challenging due to the complexity of estimating cluster assignment probabilities across views.
summary_en.method: A latent simplex position model is proposed, treating similarity matrices as rough first-stage estimates and refining them via Kullback-Leibler divergence minimization to obtain low-rank simplex coordinates that encode uncertainty.
summary_en.result: The method yields more interpretable clustering results on high-dimensional gene expression data from a traumatic brain injury study compared to single-view approaches.
summary_en.validation: Validated on a real-world high-dimensional gene expression dataset from human traumatic brain injury study.
